chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn al-Warraq) from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram who needs various types of clothing to wear; he said: 'For each type of it, there is a ransom (fidyah) upon him.'
And if the person in Ihram is compelled to wear the two socks (khuffayn) and the two stockings (jawrabayn), let him wear them, and there is no penalty upon him; he narrated that.

key_terms.الْخُفَّيْنِ: The two socks (leather or thick cloth socks worn over feet)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.اِضْطُرَّ: Was compelled or forced by necessity
key_terms.فِدَاءٌ: Ransom or compensation paid for breaking a restriction

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in Ihram who wears socks or stockings out of necessity?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the distinction is made between voluntary or standard clothing needs, which require a specific ransom (fidyah) for each type, and genuine necessity (idtirar) for footwear, which is excused without penalty. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the severity of the penalty correlates with the degree of deviation from the ideal state of Ihram, reflecting the balance between ritual purity and practical human needs.
